output.brief: First-contact resolution fell because of the Finance credit-limit change made on 14 April, not because of the new starters. That change cut the amount an agent can credit on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% that same week. Referred calls resolve first time only about 34% of the time, against 82% for the rest. Customers then call back to ask where their case is. The April intake refers at the same rate as veteran agents (56% against 53–54%), and veteran FCR fell by the same amount. The IVR change came after the drop. The tariff increase raised the share of tariff calls, which resolve well. I'm fairly confident in this. I did not check workload or occupancy data directly. Do not put the April intake on performance plans. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Compare FCR and the rate of unsupported credits against the 1% threshold the financial controller named. Don't roll it out to everyone at once. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. Get Management Information to run the team-level breakdowns as needed. A three-month dashboard rebuild is lower priority.
